property_summary: After two newGrantProposal calls (proposalCount=3) and a cancelProposal(oldProposalID=2, newProposalID=3), reference proposalCount remains 3 while buggy (proposalCount+=2) proposalCount becomes 4.

After one newGrantProposal call (proposalCount becomes 2 in reference, 3 in buggy), then a cancelProposal(oldProposalID=2, newProposalID=3) call (which reverts in reference because newProposalID does not exist, but succeeds in buggy because proposalCount=3 exists), the proposalCount value differs between reference and buggy versions.

After creating one proposal via newAddressProposal (proposalCount becomes 2 in P, 3 in M), then creating another via newGrantProposal (proposalCount becomes 3 in P, 4 in M), then calling cancelProposal(oldProposalID=1, newProposalID=3), the reference P passes (does not revert) while the buggy M reverts because mapPID_type[3] is empty (since M skipped index 2), causing isEqual to revert via low-level call to sha256 on empty bytes.
After calling cancelProposal with a specific sequence, the reference contract changes VADER to _vader while the buggy contract sets VADER to address(0), causing a divergence in the VADER() getter.

After cancelProposal(1,2) with coolOffPeriod=0, the reference contract sets mapPID_finalising[1]=true and emits ProposalFinalising, while the buggy contract having coolOffPeriod=0 prevents voting from meeting quorum/majority but cancelProposal still passes; the difference manifests in the value of USDV state variable after the call (P.USDV() != M.USDV()) due to different execution paths.

After calling cancelProposal(1,2) with coolOffPeriod=0 and a proposal that fails quorum, the reference contract does not change USDV while the buggy one changes USDV due to different finalisation logic.

After creating two GRANT proposals, voting such that proposal 1 has quorum but not majority, and proposal 2 has minority, calling cancelProposal(1,2) when coolOffPeriod=0 causes the reference to revert (because proposal 1 is not finalising) but the buggy contract to succeed, leaving mapPID_votes[1]=0 in reference but nonzero in buggy.

With coolOffPeriod=0, cancelProposal(1,2) succeeds in the buggy version (proposal 1 is finalising because coolOffPeriod=0 makes the cool off period zero) but fails in the reference (coolOffPeriod=1 means the cool off period has not elapsed yet), causing USDV state variable to remain unchanged in reference and change in the buggy version after the call.

After creating a GRANT proposal, voting to make it finalising, then calling cancelProposal on it with a new proposal that lacks minority, the reference contract reverts (cancelProposal requires hasMinority on the new proposal, which fails) while the buggy contract with coolOffPeriod=0 does not revert, leading to different USDV state after the call.

After init(VADER, USDV, VAULT) is called, calling cancelProposal(1,2) will fail on reference because old proposal is not finalising, but on mutant it reverts because VAULT is zero address (never set), causing totalWeight() call to fail.

After init(VADER, USDV, VAULT) is called, then newGrantProposal(alice, 100) and newGrantProposal(bob, 100) are called, then voteProposal(1) causes countMemberVotes to call getMemberWeight(msg.sender) on VAULT; in the reference VAULT is set, but in the mutant VAULT is never set (zero address), so getMemberWeight fails with revert. The test checks that calling voteProposal(1) does not revert on reference but reverts on mutant.

After initializing the contract, calling cancelProposal on a proposal that is finalising with an overwhelming minority new proposal succeeds in the reference (VAULT is set) but reverts in the mutant because VAULT is zero address, causing totalWeight() to fail.

After init is called, calling cancelProposal on a finalising proposal whose type matches a new proposal that has minority succeeds on reference (VAULT is set) but reverts on mutant because VAULT is never set, causing totalWeight() to fail.

After init() and creating two proposals of the same type, making the first finalising, then calling cancelProposal(1,2) succeeds on reference but reverts on mutant because VAULT is never set and totalWeight() fails on zero address call.

After init() sets VAULT = address(0) in the bug, calling cancelProposal(1,2) causes the buggy contract to revert at hasMinority(2) because VAULT is zero, while the reference contract succeeds and emits CancelProposal.
After a call to cancelProposal with oldProposalID=1 and newProposalID=2, the coolOffPeriod state variable is 1 in the reference but 2 in the buggy version.

After calling cancelProposal(1,2) with proposal 1 having majority, the reference coolOffPeriod=1 remains but the buggy coolOffPeriod=100 is still set, causing the subsequent finaliseProposal(1) to pass in reference but fail in bug due to block.timestamp difference.

After a grant proposal (ID 1) fails quorum, is voted to finalising, and then the caller tries finaliseProposal immediately, the reference P (coolOffPeriod=1) allows finalization via grantFunds if block.timestamp difference > 1, while the buggy M (coolOffPeriod=100) reverts because the timestamp difference is less than 100.

A grant proposal becomes finalising at t=0 with coolOffPeriod=1 (reference) or 100 (bug); calling finaliseProposal at t=2 succeeds for reference (due to coolOffPeriod=1) but reverts for bug (due to coolOffPeriod=100), causing a revert difference.

Proposal 1 becomes finalising at block.timestamp=0; then at block.timestamp=2, finaliseProposal(1) succeeds in reference (coolOffPeriod=1) because block.timestamp > coolOffPeriod, but reverts in buggy version (coolOffPeriod=100) because block.timestamp is not greater than 100.

A grant proposal becomes finalising at block.timestamp=0; at block.timestamp=2, finaliseProposal(1) succeeds in reference (coolOffPeriod=1) because 2 > 1, but reverts in buggy version (coolOffPeriod=100) because 2 is not greater than 100.

After `cancelProposal(1,2)` is called on a proposal with ID=1 that is finalising and proposal with ID=2 that meets the minority threshold, the reference contract retains the original proposed address at `mapPID_address[1]` while the buggy contract zeroes it, causing `c.mapPID_address(1)` to differ.

When a newAddressProposal is created with a non-zero proposed address, then later another newAddressProposal of the same type is created and the first is finalised, after cancelProposal(1,2) the reference contract retains the original address at mapPID_address[1] while the buggy contract zeroes it.

After creating an address proposal and then cancelling it, the reference contract stores the proposed address in mapPID_address, while the buggy mutant does not store it at all, causing cancelProposal to emit an event referencing an absent address.

After creating a DAO type address proposal and immediately voting (which finalises it), then creating a second address proposal and calling cancelProposal(oldProposalID=1, newProposalID=2), the reference contract correctly updates mapPID_votes[1] to 0 due to the cancel, while the buggy mutant (missing the mapPID_address assignment) does not store the proposed address for proposal 1, but the cancel still executes because it only checks mapPID_finalising[oldProposalID] and mapPID_type equality; the divergence is in mapPID_address[1] after cancelProposal returns.
